For restaurants, cafés and pubs

Social media for restaurants, cafés and pubs

Before they book, plenty of people look you up on Instagram or Facebook. Here is what is worth posting through the year, the rules that apply to food and drink posts, and how Kanosena can write a week of posts from your own website for you to approve.

Request early access See an example week

Free while we test with our first businesses. Nothing is posted until you approve it.

What’s worth posting

Posts that give people a reason to visit, and a reason to come back.

  • Specials and new dishes

    Show the plate, say what is in it and when it is on. A weekly special gives people a reason to come back and a reason to follow you.

  • Opening hours and changes

    Bank holiday hours, a private event, a closed kitchen. Posting changes early saves wasted journeys and phone calls.

  • The people behind the counter

    Your chef, your barista, the Saturday team. Faces build trust faster than food photos alone. Ask before you post anyone.

  • Booking reminders

    Sunday lunch, Mothering Sunday, Christmas parties. Remind people early, with a clear way to book.

  • Where your food comes from

    The bakery that makes your bread, the farm behind your eggs. Only say it while it is true.

  • Events and what is on

    Quiz nights, live music, the big match, tasting evenings. Give the date, the time and whether people need to book.

Your year at a glance

Moments in the UK calendar worth planning posts around.

January
Veganuary and Dry January: good months for plant-based dishes and alcohol-free drinks. Burns Night (25 January) matters most in Scotland.
February and March
Valentine’s Day (14 February), Pancake Day (Shrove Tuesday), and the Six Nations for pubs that show the rugby.
March or April
Mothering Sunday falls three weeks before Easter Sunday, and tables go quickly. Start reminding people two or three weeks ahead.
May to August
Bank holiday weekends, outdoor seating, Father’s Day (the third Sunday in June) and the school holidays.
September to November
Christmas party bookings start early. Halloween and Bonfire Night (5 November) suit themed menus and events.
December
Opening hours over Christmas and New Year, gift vouchers, and last-minute tables.

Rules worth knowing

Social media posts are advertising, so the usual rules apply. These are the ones that come up most in your line of work.

  • Drinks posts have their own rules

    The UK advertising code (the CAP Code, section 18) says alcohol marketing must not suggest that drinking makes people more confident or popular, must not encourage excessive drinking, and must not show anyone drinking who is, or looks, under 25.

    CAP Code section 18: Alcohol (ASA)

  • Only say “gluten-free” if it is

    Only food with 20 parts per million of gluten or less can be called gluten-free. If you can’t be sure a dish meets that, say what it leaves out instead of using the label.

    Gluten and the law (Coeliac UK)

  • Offers must match the till

    If a post mentions a deal or a price, say what it includes and when it ends, and make sure people pay what the post says.

  • Ask before you post people

    Get a customer’s or a team member’s agreement before you post a photo of them, and take extra care with children.

General information, checked on 27/11/2026. It isn’t legal advice: check with the body named for your own situation.

How Kanosena helps

You approve. We handle the rest.

  • We read your websiteWe build a short profile of your business, and every fact shows where it came from. You can edit any of it.
  • We write your weekPosts and simple branded graphics in your colours, written only from your profile, with UK dates and seasons in mind.
  • You approve every postApprove, edit, reject or ask for a new version. Only the posts you approve are scheduled.
  • We post and report backApproved posts go out to your Facebook Page, Instagram business account or LinkedIn Page, and we show you how they did.

Questions

Will you post offers or prices I haven’t mentioned?

No. Posts are written from what your own website says. If a price or an offer isn’t there, it won’t appear in a post. You can add details to your business profile at any time.

Can I change a post before it goes out?

Yes. Edit any word, reject a post or ask for a new version. Only the posts you approve are scheduled, and you can change or cancel a scheduled post before it goes out.

Do I need to take photos?

No. Each post comes with a simple branded graphic in your own colours, so you have something to post every week even when there is no time for photos.
